messages:
maya: Hey all — opened a docs PR that adds a short 'staged HSM provider rollout' section to the private installer guide. It covers fallback behavior (software key fallback), minimal firewall examples, and two small SDK snippets (Go + Node) showing PKCS#11 usage. PTAL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5422 :github:
doc-ryan: Nice scope. Two requests: 1) keep the staged-rollout checklist prescriptive (steps + expected smoke tests), 2) add a one-line security callout about never deploying fallback keys without approvals.
carl: Adding the checklist now. My proposed 6-step rollout flow (compact):
- Stage provider RPM in offline artifact and verify GPG/SHA256
- Deploy to a non-prod bastion and update proxy config to reference new PKCS11 URI
- Run smoke handshakes (openssl s_client) and automated health checks
- Enable staged rollout (10% of proxies) with monitoring for handshake failures
- If failures > threshold, toggle config to use local software key and collect logs
- After fix, roll forward to 100% and record provider version + GPG fingerprint

maya: Love it. Add exact smoke commands and a 3-bullet troubleshooting block. Keep everything copy-pasteable.
carl: Smoke commands to paste: `openssl s_client -connect localhost:443 -servername service.internal -showcerts` and `curl --resolve service.internal:443:127.0.0.1 https://service.internal/health -v`. Troubleshooting bullets (3):
- tcpdump/tshark on proxy to confirm ClientHello SNI is forwarded
- check proxy logs for PKCS#11 engine errors (label/slot mismatches)
- verify provider RPM signature + kernel module compatibility in system logs

doc-ryan: For the security line: add this exact sentence: \"Do not enable software fallback keys in production without an approved change and recorded justification; always verify offline package signatures.\"
sec: +1. Also ask to add a one-liner about HSM non-exportable keys and config: \"If the HSM enforces non-exportable keys, configure your TLS stack to use the PKCS#11 provider via engine integration (OpenSSL engine_pkcs11 or NSS module) instead of exporting private keys.\"
maya: Will add that. Now the SDK snippets — trying to keep them minimal. Carl, can you drop the Go example? Make it a 3-line idiomatic snippet showing pkcs11 URI use with a hypothetical TLS wrapper.

carl: Sure, paste-ready Go snippet (very small):
```go
// tls config using PKCS#11 key (pseudocode)
pkcs11URI := \"pkcs11:token=acme;object=bastion-key\"
tlsConfig := tlsconfig.FromPKCS11URI(pkcs11URI) // example helper in our SDK
server := &http.Server{Addr: \":443\", TLSConfig: tlsConfig}
server.ListenAndServeTLS(\"\", \"\")
```

maya: And a Node example? Keep it tiny and show PKCS11 URI in config for a proxy that uses node-tls with engine binding.

doc-ryan: Node snippet (pseudocode):
```js
// proxy TLS options
const pkcs11 = 'pkcs11:token=acme;object=bastion-key'
const tlsOpts = { key: { pkcs11Uri: pkcs11 }, cert: fs.readFileSync('cert.pem') }
proxy.createServer(tlsOpts, handler).listen(443)
```

maya: Great — those are distinct from current docs which mostly list URIs but not SDK examples. Add a short paragraph explaining these are pseudocode and vendor-specific adapters exist.

ops-bot: CI for PR #5422  docs-linter: passed, linkcheck: failed (1 moved anchor to hsm-rotation). See: https://ci.redwood/links/5422
maya: Which anchor? I'll replace the old rotation link with the new 'hsm-key-rotation-v2.md' anchor and add a redirect note.

doc-ryan: Also include a tiny nftables example for the proxy host (different wording than earlier docs):
```bash
# nftables minimal accept on 443 + loopback
nft add table inet redwood
nft 'add chain inet redwood input { type filter hook input priority 0; }'
nft 'add rule inet redwood input ct state established,related accept'
nft 'add rule inet redwood input iifname \"lo\" accept'
nft 'add rule inet redwood input tcp dport 443 counter accept'
```

sec: One security add: include a one-line about recording the provider GPG fingerprint in your change ticket so ops can verify during rollback.

maya: Added that sentence to the checklist. Pushing update and fixing the moved link. Re-running CI.

ops-bot: CI for PR #5422  all checks passed :white_check_mark:
doc-ryan: LGTM, I'll merge after a quick manual review. Nice work adding SDK snippets — should help customers embed PKCS#11 usage in code.
maya: Thanks everyone! I'll follow up with a short note in the install playbook template to reference this rollout flow. :rocket:
